examples: Carry a laptop to a coffee shop: it falls off the home network, finds its main again through the relay, and the pack page says via relay until it is back on a direct link.
Turn off the machine that is main for a few minutes and the first computer you opted in steps up, limited, until the original is back.
Reorder who steps up first and opt a computer out of ever taking over.
Take over from a stopped alpha on a member among the first 16 computers.
how_to: Open pack, computers, then the pack settings panel on the right: the reconnect and takeover section holds the switches and the successor order.
Turn on use the relay when the direct link is gone to let a computer reach its main through carnivore.ai when the direct link is down (the weaker protection note sits at that switch).
Turn on take over when main is gone on a computer, then opt computers in with the switch beside each name and move them up or down; only main edits the order.

When this computer follows a takeover main it says read only until you confirm; press confirm new main on each computer that should follow it. The original main takes the role back by itself once it is linked and stable for 5 minutes.
A takeover is read from the signed v2 computer list; only the first 16 computers can claim a takeover, the rest follow it.
media_exempt: The section needs a live pack of two or more computers, one of them cut off from its main, to show the state lines and the order; the capture is recorded with the release run; recaptured after the next version bump
name: Pack reconnect and takeover
summary: a computer that falls off its main finds its way back by the relay or a LAN beacon, and if main stays gone an opted-in successor takes over with limited powers until the original returns, with no vote and no outside service.
where: Pack, computers tab, pack settings panel (the gear in the title strip), section reconnect and takeover.
